Subject: Dedicated environment — question on backups and physical locality

Rachel — thanks again for the demo. A few follow-ups from our security team: we need clarity on the following for any Dedicated pool we contract for Novacorp:

1) When you say "pinned to a US region", does that apply to all persisted artifacts (logs, backups, snapshots, replication)?
2) Are automatic backups or snapshots ever replicated to other regions for HA? If so, what controls exist to opt-out?
3) For deletion/purge requests, can you provide a machine-readable audit (timestamp + job id + affected object ids) showing the deletion occurred?
4) For backups, what's the retention window and how quickly do we get proof of purge if we ask for an erasure?

We're preparing this for our legal and infosec review — concise answers and any supporting artifacts would help us move forward.

Thanks,

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then I attach the dataflow map and a sample purge log for reference.

1) "Region pinning" applies to all customer data surfaces we persist for Dedicated: model cache artifacts tied to tenant, user-uploaded payloads, request/response logs (when enabled), and backups/snapshots. We provision the Dedicated pool in a single cloud region (e.g., us-west-2) and do not cross-replicate those artifacts by default.

2) Automatic backups/snapshots: by default backups are stored in the same cloud region as the Dedicated capacity. Cross-region replication is available as an opt-in add-on only for customers who enable "multi-region HA"; for Novacorp we can disable that and keep backups region-local.

3) Deletion evidence: yes — we provide a deletion job report that includes job id, start/end timestamps, object ids (hashes for persisted blobs), and the agent node that executed the job. See attached sample (wipe-job-log-20280727.csv). We can also provide the corresponding storage provider delete receipts where available.

4) Retention and purge timeline: standard snapshot retention configurable by contract (30/90/365 days). Once you request an erasure, our pipeline will: (a) mark objects for immediate logical deletion, (b) schedule the physical purge job (depending on snapshot lifecycle) within 24–72 hours, and (c) run a verification pass that produces the audit CSV within 5 business days. If you need accelerated purge for compliance reasons we can contract for a 48-hour SLA.

I'll loop Karthik and Marissa for technical confirmation and to attach the network/dataflow diagram.

Best,

Daniel — adding the technical details you asked for.

- Storage topology: Dedicated tenant data lives in tenant-scoped buckets/volumes that are tagged with a single-region placement. We create IAM policies that restrict any automation role from performing cross-region copy unless explicitly granted on the customer contract.

- Snapshots/backups: snapshots are incremental and stored in the same region. We do not enable cross-region replication unless the customer enables the "multi-region HA" flag. For Novacorp, we'll leave that disabled; notes will be reflected in the onboarding manifest.

- Backups retention semantics:
  * Incremental snapshots: retained per the retention window.
  * Full snapshots: retained per the same policy; deletion of the last full snapshot triggers dependent incremental cleanup.

- Purge process and verification:
  * Step 1 — logical delete: metadata pointer removed and object marked for purge (immediate).
  * Step 2 — physical purge job: runs on the storage tier, removes object bytes (we issue provider delete, then verify via a HEAD/GET to ensure 404).
  * Step 3 — verification: cryptographic hashes are compared against pre-delete manifest and results exported to CSV.

- Edge cases: if a legal hold exists we can block purge; cross-tenant snapshots are not permitted. Backup replicas used for internal infra HA (control plane backups) never include customer data.

I'll export an onboarding manifest and a scoped SOC2 evidence bundle for the Dedicated pool and drop the links. If helpful, we can book a short call with our infra ops to show the wipe job in staging.

Thanks,
Karthik
